top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Munsterland Giro's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
78 miles on flat to gently rolling paved roads through the burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
When someone attacks on flat to gently rolling paved roads through the, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.

Road-specific control matters at Munsterland Giro. Practice on flat to gently rolling paved roads through the: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 78 miles.
Munsterland Giro's flat to gently rolling paved roads through the rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Munsterland Giro. Train it until it feels boring.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 3,711ft of climbing on flat to gently rolling paved roads through the does to your power file on race day.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on flat to gently rolling paved roads through the can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
At Munsterland Giro, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Munsterland Giro. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Base fitness for Munsterland Giro. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan for Munsterland Giro's 78 miles. Start early and use products you tolerate. Use the organizer's current resupply plan for final carry decisions.
